edges.description: Reproduces photoreceptor patterning and electrophysiology defects from the human substitutions in the conserved orthologue.
edges.limitations: The fly compound eye differs from the vertebrate retina, with no rod-cone distinction and no retinal pigment epithelium, so the rod-first course of the human disease cannot be tested.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characterization of Retinitis Pigmentosa Associated With Variants in SNRNP200.
evidence.snippet: Retinal imaging studies and electroretinography findings were typical of a rod-predominant dystrophy with later involvement of cone photoreceptors.

nodes.description: In human cells, losing wild-type Brr2 increases use of a cryptic 5' splice site at the expense of the correct one, and the RP mutants cannot restore correct site choice, so the variants impair Brr2's role in 5' splice-site recognition. Which retinal transcripts are affected has not been mapped.

evidence.reference_title: Retinitis pigmentosa mutations of SNRNP200 enhance cryptic splice-site recognition.
evidence.snippet: Proper splicing of optimal and cryptic splice sites was restored in cells expressing BRR2-wt but not in cells expressing RP mutants.

evidence.reference_title: Retinitis pigmentosa mutations of SNRNP200 enhance cryptic splice-site recognition.
evidence.snippet: Taken together, our data suggest that BRR2 is an important factor in 5'-splice-site recognition and that the RP-linked mutations c.3260C>T (p.S1087L) and c.3269G>T (p.R1090L) affect this BRR2 function.

nodes.description: RP variants weaken Brr2 RNA binding, ATPase and helicase activity and alter how Brr2 contacts U4 and U6 in the spliceosome, so U4/U6 is unwound inefficiently at activation. The mutant protein still assembles into snRNPs and spliceosomes, so this is an altered-function defect within the machine rather than a shortage of it.

evidence.reference_title: Retinitis Pigmentosa Mutations in Bad Response to Refrigeration 2 (Brr2) Impair ATPase and Helicase Activity.
evidence.snippet: The Δ247-Brr2 RP mutants exhibit a gradient of severity of weakened RNA binding, reduced helicase activity, and reduced ATPase activity compared with wild type Δ247-Brr2.

evidence.reference_title: Retinitis pigmentosa-linked mutations impair the snRNA unwinding activity of SNRNP200 and reduce pre-mRNA binding of PRPF8.
evidence.snippet: The significantly broader binding profile of mutated SNRNP200 within the U4 region upstream of the U4/U6 stem I strongly suggests that its activity to unwind snRNAs is impaired.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant retinitis pigmentosa caused by a mutation in SNRNP200, a gene required for unwinding of U4/U6 snRNAs.
evidence.snippet: marked defects in U4/U6 unwinding, but not U4/U6-U5 snRNP assembly, were observed in budding yeast for the analogous mutations (N1104L and R1107L) of the corresponding Brr2p residues

evidence.reference_title: Retinitis pigmentosa mutations of SNRNP200 enhance cryptic splice-site recognition.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in BRR2 did not compromise snRNP assembly and both mutants were incorporated into the spliceosome just as the wild-type (wt) protein.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characterization of Retinitis Pigmentosa Associated With Variants in SNRNP200.
evidence.snippet: each presented with nyctalopia, typically in the first 2 decades of life, although 2 patients experienced symptom onset in middle age

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-Phenotype Analysis of a Novel Recessive and a Recurrent Dominant SNRNP200 Variant Causing Retinitis Pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: Nyctalopia and photophobia were reported by 6/6 and 2/6 patients, respectively.

nodes.description: Rods fail first and cones later. In Drosophila carrying human RP substitutions in Snrnp200, photoreceptors are mispatterned and electrophysiologically abnormal, with mitochondrial defects and altered redox-gene expression; in zebrafish, the mutant but not the wild-type human protein injures the retina.

evidence.reference_title: N-acetylcysteine suppresses retinal defects in Drosophila models of SNRNP200-associated retinitis pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: When human RP-causing mutations were modeled in Drosophila Snrnp200, they resulted in abnormal retinal electrophysiology and defective patterning of photoreceptors.

evidence.reference_title: N-acetylcysteine suppresses retinal defects in Drosophila models of SNRNP200-associated retinitis pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: Further analysis of the photoreceptors revealed mitochondrial defects and altered expression of genes related to redox homeostasis.

evidence.reference_title: SNRNP200 Mutations Cause Autosomal Dominant Retinitis Pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: Overexpression of SNRNP200Arg2030Cys, but not SNRNP200WT caused systemic deformities in the wild-type zebrafish embryos with the retina primarily injured

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characterization of Retinitis Pigmentosa Associated With Variants in SNRNP200.
evidence.snippet: Retinal imaging studies and electroretinography findings were typical of a rod-predominant dystrophy with later involvement of cone photoreceptors.

meta.association: Causative heterozygous missense variants, mostly in the first helicase cassette.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant retinitis pigmentosa caused by a mutation in SNRNP200, a gene required for unwinding of U4/U6 snRNAs.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report the identification of a missense mutation, c.3260C>T (p.S1087L), in exon 25 of the SNRNP200 gene in an RP33-linked family.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ASCC3L1 on 2q11.2 are associated with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of ASCC3L1 in an affected family member showed a heterozygous single-base-pair change; c.3269G-->T, predicted to result in an Arg1090Leu amino acid change.
SNRNP200 | HGNC:30859 | SNRNP200-related dominant retinopathy | MONDO:0800098 | AD | Definitive

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants concentrate in exons 16 and 25. The recurrent p.Ser1087Leu and p.Arg1090Leu lie in the ratchet helix of the first Sec63 domain, which governs directional unwinding.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal-dominant retinitis pigmentosa caused by a mutation in SNRNP200, a gene required for unwinding of U4/U6 snRNAs.
evidence.snippet: The p.S1087L mutation and p.R1090L, another adRP-associated allele, reside in the "ratchet" helix of the first of two Sec63 domains implicated in the directionality and processivity of nucleic acid unwinding.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the small nuclear riboprotein 200 kDa gene (SNRNP200) cause 1.6% of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenic mutations were found primarily in exons 16 and 25
